title: 4541007B-Need_for_Speed_Most_Wanted.xiso.iso
queue_order: Queued by the lane under the hard 4-run/500s cap (one enqueue, batched with the texscan census below). b_ref (81ab5f3418) is a_ref (9c8b1b12b6) plus ONE line: NFS Most Wanted (4541007B) added to kTitleRenderModes as sysmem. Off gets ONE fresh run here (the brief's '2 runs per arm' is not affordable on a 4-run cap once step 3's census also needs a slot on a_ref): request.sh --who gpupass1010 --title <title> --route nfs-mw-quickrace --seconds 500 --device nova --ref 9c8b1b12b6 --env HAKUX_GPUXFR=1 --expect this file. On gets TWO fresh runs, same command with --ref 81ab5f3418, since it is the new/uncertain finding. Off is backstopped, not replaced, by lane.nfs30plan1010's existing XFR rpc census on the pre-texscan, pre-row code (runs 1-1791649387/1-1791649388, NOTES.md 5.5): those runs cite the same render-mode default (GMEM, no table row for NFS existed before this lane) so they corroborate a_ref's cold figures without being on a_ref's exact sha.
judge: python3 docs/lanes/gpupass1010/gpuread.py <off run dir> --arm off --expect docs/testing/predictions/gpupass1010-rendermode.json ; python3 docs/lanes/gpupass1010/gpuread.py <on run dir 1> <on run dir 2> --arm on --expect docs/testing/predictions/gpupass1010-rendermode.json
baseline: lane.nfs30plan1010's XFR rpc census (runs 1-1791649387/1-1791649388, NOTES.md 5.5), GMEM default, no table row: GPU busy 21.7 ms/frame cold / 12.8 warm, 69 render passes/frame cold / 26.5 warm, 24.9 pass pairs, 20 MB GMEM load + 20 MB store, PFIFO on-CPU cold frame 56-62 ms (GPU not on the path today). The corpus (gmem474/rendermode474/flip474): sysmem cut GPU time 60.0->28.6 ms on DOA and 40.1->21.5 on AUF (both had X/R ~1 under GMEM, i.e. the draw stream ran twice); Kabuki did not win (X/R stayed 0.77, GMEM already near-sysmem there). No lane measured NFS's X/R under either mode before this one.
prediction: #433 step 1: NFS MW's race-start GPU frame, sysmem vs the GMEM default. GMEM mode re-runs the draw stream once per bin/tile; the corpus's two wins (DOA, AUF) both started from X/R ~1 (full double run) and sysmem collapsed it toward 0, roughly halving GPU busy. NFS's own X/R has never been measured, so the headline (G, X legs) is a conditional prediction, not a certainty: IF NFS behaves like AUF/DOA (X/R ~1 under GMEM), cold GPU busy falls from 21.7 to <= 14 ms/frame and X/R falls to roughly 0 under sysmem. The falsifier is M: if the on arm's in/out ratio stays below 0.8 (draw.c's own GMEM-still-active threshold), sysmem did not actually take effect (env ordering bug, or TU_DEBUG already named a mode) and G/X cannot be read as a render-mode effect at all. Passes/frame (the P leg here, cold) should be roughly UNCHANGED by the mode switch alone -- sysmem and GMEM both bin the same draw stream into the same command-buffer/pass structure per the pgraph code; mode changes how a pass is tiled and replayed, not how many passes the frame issues (that count is step 3's variable, texscan's cube-face traffic, not render mode's). PERIOD is predicted small/within the run-to-run noise band (~4-5 ms, per texscan1010's own off-arm spread) on this base: reportasync1010 (the piece that moves the occlusion-report wait off the PFIFO thread, which is what would actually expose GPU busy time to the critical path) is not yet merged here, and texscan1010's own A/B showed a GPU-busy increase (13.4->18.0 ms/frame) absorbed into existing wait slack rather than exposed as added period (Fin stayed ~constant at 12.0 ms). The falsifier for 'GPU is not on NFS's critical path today' is a period that moves with GPU busy ms, start-for-start, more than the noise band -- if the on arm's period drops by an amount tracking its GPU-busy drop, the GPU WAS on the path and this lane's own framing (quoting the brief's 'Why') is wrong for this base.
expect_note: M/G/X are left to gpuread.py's own --arm-conditional defaults rather than fixed here, because the same file is read once with --arm off and once with --arm on and the two arms need opposite M bounds (off: in/out in [0.0, 0.8], GMEM; on: in/out in [0.8, 1.5], sysmem) and different G/X caps (on: G_cold_max 14.0, X_cold_max 0.3; off: both uncapped at 99.0, since the prediction's magnitude claim is conditional on NFS behaving like AUF/DOA and only the on arm's G/X are claimed, not the off arm's). A fixed numeric override in this dict would apply to BOTH arm invocations identically and silently break that split. Named rules read by docs/lanes/gpupass1010/gpuread.py (legs V, M, G, X, P); period and the on-vs-off pass-count/GPU-ms deltas are read by hand in NOTES.md from the two --arm invocations' POOLED lines, because gpuread.py judges one arm per invocation and does not itself diff across arms.
